label: copy-phase input u at the first or second copy step
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input is the letter u and it is early in the copy: recall_idx 1 (u is original token 0, input right after <DEL>) or recall_idx 2 (u is original token 1). Magnitude is strongly set by position: when orig(0)=u it fires at about 0.85-1.0 of max (81% of the mass); when u comes in at recall_idx 2 it is much weaker, about 0.1-0.4 of max, and it is often silent there in short sequences (most false positives). It does not fire on u in the original phase, on u later in the copy (recall_idx >= 3), or on any other token (other tokens hold less than 0.1% of the mass). It does not depend on the output token or L.

issues: The false positives are not random. They all come from short sequences at recall_idx 2. On the test split, at recall_idx 2 with in_tok=u, precision is 0.0 for L=3 (421 steps predicted), 0.41 for L=4 (2395 steps), and 1.0 for every L>=5. When L=4 does fire there, the activation is tiny (about 0.02-0.08 of max), essentially threshold noise. The explanation does say the feature is 'often silent there in short sequences', so the claim holds, but the predicate does not encode it.

The other claims check out. Mass is entirely in the copy phase. recall_idx 1 holds 81% of the mass with precision 1.0 (test). recall_idx 2 holds 19% and is weaker (example activation 0.35). recall_idx 3 has only 18 dev activations and other tokens have about 0.1% of activations. Missed activations hold 0.0% of the mass (56 steps, tiny values).
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input u at the first copy step (any L) or the second copy step (L>=5 only)
